slides.texte_overlay:
hobbies that make discipline
feel like an addiction

streak calendars

hang a paper calendar on your wall and cross off every day you do your one habit. after a week, not breaking the chain starts to feel even better than the habit itself.

two minute starts

promise yourself only two minutes of the thing you're avoiding. starting is always the hardest part, and once you've started, your brain almost always wants to finish.

a tiny daily lesson

learn one small thing every day in 5 minutes: a word, a fact, a famous painting. a habit this easy is impossible to skip, and it teaches your brain that showing up feels good.
slides.texte_sophia:
a tiny daily lesson

i learn one small thing every day in 5 minutes: a word, a fact, a painting. i do it with the Sophia app, one lesson a day, and it taught my brain that showing up feels good.

slides.texte_overlay:
morning walks

walk for 20 minutes every morning before you check your phone. starting the day with something you chose, instead of something that grabbed you, sets the tone for the rest.

a habit buddy

find one friend and send each other a photo every day you both do your habit. being seen makes it twice as hard to skip, and twice as fun when you don't skip it.
